endpoint.text: Primary endpoint: composite rate of stroke (ischemic or hemorrhagic) and systemic embolism (noninferiority to warfarin, with superiority also examined).

citations.quote: The primary objective of ARISTOTLE was to determine whether ELIQUIS 5 mg twice daily (or 2.5 mg twice daily) was effective (noninferior to warfarin) in reducing the risk of stroke (ischemic or hemorrhagic) and systemic embolism. Superiority of ELIQUIS to warfarin was also examined for the primary endpoint (rate of stroke and systemic embolism), major bleeding, and death from any cause.

result.text: Stroke/systemic embolism (ITT): 212/9120 apixaban vs 265/9081 warfarin, HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.66, 0.95), p=0.0114 (superiority). Major bleeding: HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.60, 0.80), p<0.0001. All-cause death: 603 vs 669, HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.80, 1.00), p=0.0465.

key_safety.text: The most serious and most common adverse reactions are related to bleeding. In ARISTOTLE, major bleeding occurred in 327 (2.13%/year) apixaban patients vs 462 (3.09%/year) warfarin patients (HR 0.69); intracranial bleeding 0.33% vs 0.82% (HR 0.41). Bleeding-related discontinuation occurred in 1.7% (apixaban) vs 2.5% (warfarin).

citations.quote: The most serious adverse reactions reported with ELIQUIS were related to bleeding [see *Warnings and Precautions* (5.2)].
Most common adverse reactions (>1%) are related to bleeding. (6.1)

The most common reason for treatment discontinuation in both studies was for bleeding-related adverse reactions; in ARISTOTLE this occurred in 1.7% and 2.5% of patients treated with ELIQUIS and warfarin, respectively, and in AVERROES, in 1.5% and 1.3% on ELIQUIS and aspirin, respectively.

detail.text: WARNING: DISCONTINUING ELIQUIS IN PATIENTS WITHOUT ADEQUATE CONTINUOUS ANTICOAGULATION INCREASES RISK OF STROKE. Discontinuing ELIQUIS places patients at an increased risk of thrombotic events; an increased rate of stroke was observed following discontinuation in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, and coverage with another anticoagulant should be strongly considered.

citations.quote: ## WARNING: DISCONTINUING ELIQUIS IN PATIENTS WITHOUT ADEQUATE CONTINUOUS ANTICOAGULATION INCREASES RISK OF STROKE

Discontinuing ELIQUIS places patients at an increased risk of thrombotic events. An increased rate of stroke was observed following discontinuation of ELIQUIS in clinical trials in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation. If anticoagulation with ELIQUIS must be discontinued for a reason other than pathological bleeding, coverage with another anticoagulant should be strongly considered [see *Dosage and Administration* (2.4) and *Warnings and Precautions* (5.1)].
